design_references.title: Fleet CPG Engine — Phase 3 (Prove steady-state operation)
design_references.claim: Replace full re-index on push with differential base maintenance -- a delta fixpoint over standing relations. Golden-query differential tests must pass: incremental result equals from-scratch result, on every query, after every push, with zero exceptions carved out. This is the base indexer's own correctness bar, tested for the first time as a sequence of real pushes rather than a single update -- Phases 1 and 2 held the base fixed and only tested one overlay against it.

hypothesis: Walking a real 7-commit chain on zod's own history (every commit touching packages/zod/src), maintaining one base snapshot incrementally step by step with no full re-scan after the initial build, both the L1 facts (defs, calls) and an L2 blast-radius relation computed on the incrementally-maintained base match a from-scratch full extraction at every single step, with per-step update cost that does not grow across the chain.
null_hypothesis: Any step's incrementally-maintained facts or blast-radius relation diverge from a from-scratch extraction at that commit, or per-step update cost grows as the chain progresses (indicating the base is not staying O(diff) per step, e.g. because of an accumulating error or a full-scan leaking in).
independent_variable: Chain length -- short-chain (3 commits, 2 steps) vs. full-chain (7 commits, 6 steps), both real prefixes of the same zod commit sequence -- holding the extractor, merge mechanism, and blast-radius relation fixed. Each variant repeated 3 times to check the whole chain replays deterministically.

environment.network_justification: git clone of zod from github.com (already materialized from earlier fleet-cpg-* experiments). No other endpoints.

variants.name: short-chain
variants.description: First 3 commits of the same real chain, oldest to newest: 0a69bcb3 (4.5.0) -> 8e033805 (4.5.1) -> 212b9417 (#6488). One init + 2 incremental steps per repetition. A comparison point against full-chain to check per-step cost doesn't depend on chain length.

variants.name: full-chain
variants.description: Real 7-commit chain on zod's own history, oldest to newest, every commit touching packages/zod/src: 0a69bcb3 (4.5.0) -> 8e033805 (4.5.1) -> 212b9417 (#6488) -> 9a193aa2 (4.5.2) -> eab51ff3 (#6497) -> 1a16102a (4.5.3) -> 84e416fb (#6500). One init + 6 incremental steps per repetition.

metrics.acceptance_rule: Accept: every step of every repetition has defs_match_truth, calls_match_truth, and blast_radius_match_truth all true, and median incremental_update_wall_time_ms does not trend upward across the 6 steps (a late step should cost about the same as an early one). Reject: any single mismatch anywhere in the chain, or a clear upward trend in per-step update cost.

evaluator.rubric: Score on: (1) every step of every repetition -- 6 steps per rep, walking a real 7-commit chain -- has both L1 facts (defs, calls) and the L2 blast-radius relation computed on the incrementally-maintained base matching a from-scratch full extraction at that same commit exactly; one mismatch anywhere fails the run, not just that step, since a real differential base carries a wrong state forward rather than self-healing; (2) incremental update cost per step stays small and does not grow across the chain -- a step late in the chain should cost about the same as a step early in it, since each step's cost is a function of that push's diff size, not the chain's length or the base's accumulated size; (3) the base is never fully re-scanned after the initial build -- each step's extractor call is scoped to only that push's changed files, verified structurally from the driver's own arguments, not just asserted.
